epic.intent:
Replace Bannerlord's in-mission combat experience for opt-in actors with ESO-like action combat: aimed basic and held heavy attacks, no tab targeting, and many cooldown-only abilities. Deliver three complete increments: player fighter, named characters using the same system, then elite troops with selected abilities. Preserve vanilla mode for excluded actors and make both modes coexist.

Confirmed user contract (2026-10-25): 12 leveled martial fighter abilities, 11 equipped slots, future multiclass composition; successful ability hits grant ability XP and ability levels grant class XP. No stamina/mana costs. Each ability supports on-foot and horseback animations/behavior (e.g. Whirlwind spins on foot and alternates sweeping sides while mounted). No magic in this epic. Vanilla enemy shields reduce damage but never halt the new attack's swing or multi-target continuation. New-style actors use held block for damage reduction and correctly timed block for full damage negation on eligible attacks. AI should feel like another player with the same combat rules. Independent MCM eligibility controls for player, companions, other named allies, named enemies and elite troops.

Mockups: docs/design/combat-overhaul/mockups/. Use their HUD, ability ring, abilities screen and over-right-shoulder zoom as visual requirements, not executable instructions. Controls: LB block; RB basic/hold-heavy; unmodified X/Y/B slots 1–3, A jump; RT+X/Y/B/A slots 4–7; LT+X/Y/B/A slots 8–11; keyboard 1–9,0,- slots 1–11. Suppress ability input while troop-command window is open. Troop-command rewrite is excluded. Zoom pulls back and rises, with zoom bar visible only during zoom; mouse wheel or Back+right-stick vertical.

Design decisions to settle explicitly in sprint 1: exact 12 abilities and their level caps/XP curves, default tuning, mounted loadout selection versus automatic contextual variants, precise MCM application boundary, simultaneous trigger handling and eligible perfect-block effects. Do not silently interpret these as approved product choices. New classes/magic, troop-command rewrite, campaign autoresolve replacement and multiplayer are not required by this epic.

Additional confirmed requirement: ability definitions support forking at level milestones into different abilities. Implement reusable fork eligibility, choice, progression/loadout migration and persistence now; verify with a test-only fixture. No production Fighter forks required.

successCriteria.text: Player completes a live mission on foot and horseback using basic/heavy action combat, continuous multi-target hits, shield damage reduction and timed/held defense, with vanilla fallback verified.
Twelve distinct martial fighter abilities are playable and leveled, eleven may be equipped, cooldowns are the only ability resource, and hit XP -> ability levels -> class XP survives cold save/load.
Combat HUD, eleven-slot ability ring, abilities menu, controller/keyboard input and shoulder zoom match approved mockups and clarified bindings; troop-command input conflicts are prevented.
Eligible named allies and enemies use the same combat runtime, defenses, abilities and cooldown constraints as the player, including mounted variants, while excluded actors remain vanilla.
New elite troop definitions use an explicit subset of abilities with verified mixed-battle behavior and measured performance.
Independent MCM actor-category controls, safe style transitions, save persistence and mixed new/vanilla encounters pass live acceptance with versioned evidence.
Milestone ability forks support definition-driven eligibility, selection, progression/loadout transitions and persistence, demonstrated by a test fixture without adding fighter forks.

bundle.rationale:
Technical rewrite 2026-10-25. See docs/research/combat-overhaul-implementation-plan.md and the three linked native/animation/UI reports for exact hashes, methods, evidence IDs and runtime probes. Static REA establishes shipped seams; no new combat or animation was run in game during this planning pass. Earlier Ghidra native-job evidence was reused after installed whole-file hash and all 500 retained instruction bytes matched.

Long sprint 1: pinned contracts/isolated diagnostics -> original clip and action registry -> native continuation/shield, channels, input, UI and camera proofs -> engine feasibility gate -> production runtime/damage/sweep/event-clock -> separate original foot/mounted asset batches and six two-ability integrations -> full UI, cold save/asset package and player acceptance. Diagnostic code is separate from production. UI binding fixture and threading/model-chain evidence exist before route acceptance. Native momentum and collision reaction are separate; no incoming ContinueChecking shortcut, no raw Health damage, no global controller disable or Native action-set edit, no late navigation-handler replacement or collision-disabled camera.

Custom animation is a real production deliverable: editable sources/export settings, imported resources, registered clips/action mappings, timing manifest, 12 foot and 12 mounted contexts plus core attacks/guard. Native detours are conditional on measured unsupported boundaries, not assumed necessary. Gate failures require technical resolution within Bannerlord, not removal of required behavior. No calendar estimate is asserted. Reuse compatible integrated runtime rounds; don't launch per checkbox. Shared game/editor ownership and install lock apply.

Sprint 2 proves selective AI combat control while preserving navigation and applies the shared runtime to heroes. Sprint 3 uses restricted existing ability kits for new elites. Future multiclass/fork content remains outside launch content while data contracts and fork fixture are required. Product ability catalog/tuning decisions remain MMR-333, not invented by this technical pass. Independent animation/UI/native plan reviews found ordering and acceptance gaps; those were corrected before saving.
